metric_definitions.kge: 1 - sqrt((r-1)^2 + (alpha-1)^2 + (beta-1)^2); population standard deviation ratio and mean ratio
metric_definitions.event_peak_error: Peak magnitude error is relative to the observed event-window maximum; timing error is signed predicted minus observed peak index times the declared fixed step duration. Ties select the first maximum.
metric_definitions.low_flow_log_error: Mean absolute/signed log10(flow_predicted)-log10(flow_observed) over samples whose observed flow is <= a frozen threshold; only strictly positive observed and predicted values are admitted; no pseudocount.
metric_definitions.interval_metrics: Empirical coverage is count(observed within [lower,upper])/N; width is the arithmetic mean of upper-lower; report nominal and empirical coverage, error and width.
metric_definitions.empirical_ensemble_crps: CRPS(F,y) = mean_m |x_m-y| - (1/(2M^2)) sum_m sum_n |x_m-x_n| for the finite empirical ensemble; lower is better. Report raw ensemble size and do not clip negative CRPS caused by an implementation bug.
metric_definitions.binary_event_brier: Brier score = mean_i (p_i-o_i)^2 for explicitly defined binary events, where p is a forecast probability in [0,1] and o is an observed 0/1 outcome.
metric_definitions.reliability_bins: Descriptive five fixed probability bins [0,.2), [.2,.4), [.4,.6), [.6,.8), [.8,1]; report count, mean forecast probability and observed event frequency; empty bins remain null.
metric_definitions.crps_skill_score: CRPSS = 1 - mean(CRPS_forecast)/mean(CRPS_reference), evaluated on identical observation case IDs, evaluation population and lead time. Negative scores remain negative; a zero reference score is Undefined.
metric_definitions.brier_skill_score: BSS = 1 - mean(BS_forecast)/mean(BS_reference), evaluated for the same versioned binary event, observation case IDs, evaluation population and lead time. Negative scores remain negative; a zero reference score is Undefined.
metric_definitions.crps_skill: CRPSS = 1 - mean(CRPS_forecast)/mean(CRPS_reference) over exactly the same target cases, catchment/evaluation population and forecast lead. A zero reference CRPS yields Undefined. Do not clip negative skill.
metric_definitions.brier_skill: BSS = 1 - mean(BS_forecast)/mean(BS_reference) over exactly the same binary event cases, event definition and lead. A zero reference Brier score yields Undefined. Do not clip negative skill.

rules: All data and values are synthetic; this evaluator does not generate or calibrate a hydrology model.
B0 seasonal climatology and every normalization/imputation transform must be fitted on training data only.
B1 invalid or non-conservative ensemble members must remain visible with exclusion reasons; they may not be silently hidden.
B2 repeated calibration results are in-sample references only and must not access final test targets.
B3 temporal/event holdout predictions must be frozen before the evaluator reads test observations.
Event and nested-catchment leakage are split-integrity failures unless an explicit transfer design is separately declared.
Missing, censored or unknown values are not zero discharge.
Unknown dam release, abstraction or diversion conditions require abstention or downgrade.
Timebase, calendar, timezone and aggregation semantics must match exactly.
Predictive skill cannot override a failed physical water-balance gate.
Contextual attainment is metric/task/population scoped; it is not clipped to [0,1] and must be undefined/not-comparable when references cannot support it.
Synthetic evidence may not be promoted to field or operational qualification.
The final test split may not be used to select the winning model from a tournament; model selection must use the predeclared validation process.

Peak magnitude/timing metrics are computed only on a named frozen event window with declared fixed time step; timing error is signed predicted minus observed peak time and ties choose the earliest peak.
Low-flow log10 error uses a predeclared threshold and only strictly positive observed/predicted flows; zeros are not replaced with pseudocounts and yield Indeterminate.
Probabilistic interval coverage and width are reported separately; invalid lower>upper interval rows reject the interval metric rather than being silently repaired.
Coverage/width metrics do not themselves establish probabilistic calibration across a sufficiently large event population; sample size and event strata remain mandatory.
When multiple equal maxima occur in a named event window, peak timing is assigned to the earliest time step for both observation and prediction.
Probabilistic forecasts must be scored with proper scores such as empirical ensemble CRPS for continuous flow and Brier score for declared threshold events; do not substitute interval coverage alone.
Event definitions, units, threshold, forecast lead and valid-time semantics must be frozen before evaluation; observed event labels are independently derived.
Forecast probabilities outside [0,1], non-binary outcomes, or negative streamflow ensemble values are rejected, never clipped.
Reliability bins are descriptive diagnostics; sparse bins do not establish calibration. Report sample counts and uncertainty and evaluate across multiple events, catchments and lead times.

Skill scores are relative to an explicitly identified reference and are only comparable when forecast/reference use exactly the same evaluation population, ordered observation case IDs, lead time and (for Brier) event definition.
CRPSS and BSS are not clipped to [0,1]; negative values mean the forecast is worse than the named reference.
A zero or near-zero reference score makes the corresponding skill score Undefined, not zero or infinite.
Do not compare a forecast to a reference computed on different catchments, events, observation cases, lead times or threshold definitions.
Each relative skill result names both the candidate forecast and reference forecast (for example, persistence or train-only seasonal climatology); unnamed or implicit references are not accepted.
Skill comparisons reject different ordered observation-case identities or different versioned binary-event definitions, even when aggregate sample counts match.

Skill comparisons require exact identity of target case IDs, evaluation population, variable, unit, temporal aggregation, valid-time semantics and forecast lead; binary event comparisons additionally require exact event-definition identity.

A positive skill score indicates improvement over the chosen reference; zero indicates parity; a negative score is valid evidence that the forecast is worse than the reference and must not be clipped or suppressed.
Forecast and reference scores must be computed on the same verification cases; do not compare a candidate on an easier subset or a different lead time.
The reference forecast must be named, frozen and eligible for the same valid-time information set; training-only climatology and persistence are not interchangeable reference populations.
Forecast/reference variable identities must match; a discharge forecast cannot be compared with water level or another target variable.
Forecast/reference valid-time semantics must match exactly, including timezone/day boundary and the temporal interval represented.
